ratings_why.fun: Duel bodies win the early turns, Elder and Marshal give steady mid-game growth, and three Tier 6 caps give a late game worth reaching; a few dead early buys hold it at 7.
ratings_why.distinct: Empty slots as fuel and Proud gaps make a board shape no current tribe uses; Start of Combat duels are more familiar.

verdict_why: The Chronicler's 'twice its stats' can read as doubling the Champion, and the Reisig/Hen rule clash needs one line.

points.text: 'Your Champion permanently gains twice its stats' reads as the Champion doubling itself every turn, which would be a runaway. Say 'twice the destroyed unit's stats'.
Dame Reisig says the Champion is your biggest unit of any tribe, but Champion says Hens are never Champion. Say whether Reisig, a 3/9, can crown herself or another Hen.
Refectory Prior does nothing at Tier 2, so it is a dead buy on the turn you see it. A small Tier 2 payout, such as 1 gold at 3 or fewer units, would keep it live without the old always-right problem.
Pennon-Squire's +1/+1 is thin for Tier 2; the Duel keyword is the value. Letting it pick a Proud target for +2/+2 would tie it to the second build.
The growth shape is good: Duel tempo early, Elder and Marshal mid, then Gottfried, Altmark or Ottokar. The lone Champion line still risks low hero damage when it wins, so sim it against wide boards.

standouts.why: Elder of the Centre turns the shrinking board into steady growth and makes every sell a real choice.
Sir Altmark scales with the enemy's size, not his own, so he grows hard late without feeding on himself.
Sir Gottfried is a capstone you build the whole game toward, and it pays for giving up board HP.

weakest.why: Refectory Prior is dead text until Tier 3.
Pennon-Squire gives too few stats to carry a Tier 2 slot unless you need Duel on a splash.
Grit-Pit Forager is a slow drip of stones in a tier that also offers Elder and Hartmut.

flags.note: 'twice its stats' has two readings; the Champion reading doubles it each turn.
Reisig's any-tribe Champion conflicts with the rule that Hens are never Champion.
x4 in fight on a Champion already fed by Elder, Reisig and Chronicler; counterplay is wide boards and summons.
With Herald, Hartmut and Cork-Pop, free first Duels can clear the enemy front row before anyone attacks.
